en: Dīgha Nikāya 20,
Mahāsamaya Sutta:
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Forest together with a large Saṅgha of monks, about five hundred monks, all of whom were arahants.
And from ten world-systems, deities had for the most part gathered together to see the Blessed One and the Saṅgha of monks.
Then it occurred to four deities belonging to the Pure Abodes:
“This Blessed One is dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Forest together with a large Saṅgha of monks, about five hundred monks, all of whom are arahants;
and deities from ten world-systems have for the most part assembled to see the Blessed One and the Saṅgha of monks.
What if we were also to approach the Blessed One, and having approached, each recite a verse in the presence of the Blessed One?”
Then those deities, just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, vanished from among the Suddhāvāsa deities and appeared before the Blessed One.
Then those deities paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
“A great assembly is in the grove;
the hosts of devas have gathered together.
We have come to this assembly of Dhamma.”
“For the sake of the invincible Saṅgha.
Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
“Therein the monks have concentrated their minds;”
They made their own minds straight;
like charioteers holding the reins,
the wise protect their sense faculties.
Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
“Having cut through the post, having cut through the crossbar,
having uprooted the threshold-stone, you are unshakable.”
“They wander pure and stainless,
well-tamed like noble elephants by the One with Vision.
Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
“Whoever has gone for refuge to the Buddha will not go to a plane of misery;
having cast off the human body,”
“They will fulfill the host of devas.
Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “The assembly of devas. 1. The Assembly of Devas. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: [“The assembly of devas.”]
“Bhikkhus, for the most part, the deities from ten world-systems have assembled to see the Tathāgata and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Those Blessed Ones who were the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, in the past—even for them, the deities assembled in such numbers as these, just as they have for me now.”
"Monks, whatever Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones there shall be in the future, for those Blessed Ones as well, the deities assembled will be no more than this, just as they are for me now.
Monks, I shall declare the names of the hosts of deities;
monks, I shall proclaim the names of the hosts of deities."
“Monks, I will teach you the names of the hosts of devas.
Listen to that and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
"I shall proclaim the fame of those earth-dwellers who rely upon it."
Those who dwell in mountain caves,
self-exerted and concentrated,
lie hidden like many lions.
They have overcome the horripilation [of fear];
with minds bright and pure,
they are serene and undisturbed.
Knowing that there were more than five hundred [monks] in the Kāpilavatthava forest,
the Teacher then addressed them:
“O monks, those who delight in the teaching of the disciples— know them to be superior even to the hosts of devas.”
And having heard the Buddha’s teaching, they applied themselves with ardor;
knowledge appeared to them.
The sight of non-human beings;
some indeed saw a hundred,
a thousand, or even seventy.
Some hundreds of thousands of non-human beings devoured him;
yet with even less, they saw their end.
All directions were filled [with my fame].
Having directly known all that and having established it with the eye of wisdom, the Visionary One—
Then the Teacher addressed his disciples who delight in the teaching:
“The hosts of devas have arrived.”
"Understand them, O monks;
those whom I shall proclaim in due order with words."
Those seven thousand yakkhas,
the earth-dwellers of Kapilavatthu,
possessed of psychic power and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the monks.
A thousand from the Himavat mountains,
yakkhas of diverse forms,
possessing psychic power and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
From Sātāgira came three thousand yakkhas of diverse forms,
possessed of psychic power and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
These sixteen thousand yakkhas of diverse appearances,
possessing psychic power and radiance—
Handsome and renowned,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
Five hundred Vessāmitta yakkhas of various forms,
possessed of supernormal power and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
Kumbhīra, a resident of Rājagaha,
dwells in the vicinity of Vepulla;
more than a hundred thousand [others] [dwell there as well].
He attends upon the yakkhas;
Kumbhīra of Rājagaha has come to this assembly in the forest.
In the eastern direction,
King Dhatarattha rules,
the lord of the gandhabbas.
The great king was renowned.
He had many sons,
all named Indra and possessed of great strength.
Possessing psychic power, radiant,
beautiful, and renowned,
they approached rejoicing.
The King Virūḷha rules over the southern quarter, [the forest] where the assembly of monks gathers.
The lord of the kumbhaṇḍas,
a glorious great king;
he too has many sons.
They were named Indra, possessed of great strength;
they were endowed with supernormal powers, radiant,
beautiful, and renowned.
Rejoicing, they advanced toward the forest assembly of the bhikkhus;
and the king [advanced] toward the western direction.
Virūpakkha rules as the lord of the nāgas,
a great king of great renown.
He had many sons,
all named Indra, possessed of great strength,
endowed with supernormal powers and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
And in the northern direction,
King Kuvera rules there,
the lord of the yakkhas.
He was a glorious great king.
His sons were many,
all named Indra and possessed of great strength.
Possessing psychic power, radiant,
beautiful, and renowned,
they approached rejoicing.
To the assembly of monks in the forest:
Dhataraṭṭha from the eastern direction,
and Virūḷhaka from the south.
To the west is Virūpakkha,
and Kuvera is in the northern direction.
These are the four Great Kings.
Shining brilliantly, they stood on all four sides in the Kāpilavatthava forest.
To them came deceitful slaves,
tricksters, and rogues:
Māyā, Kuṭeṇḍu, and Viṭeṇḍu.
Viṭucca and Viṭuṭa together,
Candana and Kāmaseṭṭha,
Kinnighaṇḍu and Nighaṇḍu;
Panāda and Opamañña,
Mātali the charioteer of the gods,
and the Gandhabba Cittasena.
King Nala and Janesabha,
as well as Pañcasikha,
Timbaru, and Suriyavaccasā, arrived.
These kings and others,
along with the gandhabbas and their rulers,
approached while rejoicing.
To the forest gathering of the monks,
there came the Nāgasā and the Nāgas,
the Vesālīans together with the Sahatacchakas.
The Kambalas and Assataras arrived,
as did the Pāyāgas with their kinsmen,
along with the Yāmunas and Dhataraṭṭhas.
The renowned Nāgas have arrived;
the great Nāga Erāvaṇa has come to this forest assembly.
The divine birds with pure vision, who suddenly carry away the Naga kings,
having reached the middle of the forest through the air.
"Citrā" and "Supaṇṇā" were their names.
At that time, the Buddha granted fearlessness to the Naga kings and made them safe from the Supaṇṇas.
Addressing him with gentle words,
the nāgas and supaṇṇas took refuge in the Buddha,
who was victorious over those with thunderbolt-hands.
The Asuras and Asitā are like the ocean;
these brothers of Vāsava are possessed of supernatural power and great renown.
Kālakañca and Mahābhisma,
the Asuras Dānava and Ighasa,
Vepacitti and Sucitti—
Pahārāda together with Namuci,
and the hundred sons of Bali,
all of whom were named Veroca;
Having equipped their army,
they approached the auspicious Rāhu, saying:
"The time has now come, O Blessed One."
To the assembly of monks in the forest,
the deities of water, earth,
fire, and wind then came.
The Varuṇa and Vāraṇa deities,
Soma together with Yaśas,
and the bodily [states of] loving-kindness and compassion.
The glorious gods have come;
these ten groups, each consisting of ten,
are all of diverse appearances.
Possessing psychic power, radiant,
beautiful, and renowned,
they approached while rejoicing.
To the assembly of monks in the forest came the gods Veṇḍu and Sahali,
and the two Asamas and Yamās.
The deities who have the moon as their support came,
placing the moon in front of them; the deities who have the sun as their support [came, placing the sun in front of them].
The sun has arrived,
preceded by the constellations;
the gentle clouds have arrived, preceded by the stars.
Vāsava is the best of the Vasus;
Sakka, the first-born, has arrived.
These ten [classes] are the tenfold hosts.
All were of diverse complexions,
possessed of psychic power, radiant,
beautiful, and glorious.
Rejoicing, they approached the forest assembly of the bhikkhus;
then the Sahabhū deities arrived.
Like flames of water and fire;
and the Ariṭṭhakas and Rojas,
resembling the color of flax flowers.
Varuṇa, Sahadhamma,
Accuta, and Anejaka,
along with Sūleyya and Rucira, have arrived.
The dwellers in the realm of Vāsava have arrived;
these ten groups, each consisting of ten,
are all of diverse appearances.
Possessing psychic power, radiant,
beautiful, and renowned,
they approached while rejoicing.
To the forest gathering of the monks—
those great recluses who are human and the best among humans.
The gods corrupted by play arrived;
the gods corrupted by mind arrived;
then the Haris gods arrived.
And those who dwell in the Red Abode,
the Pāragas and Mahāpāragas—
those renowned deities have come.
These ten groups of ten bodies,
all of diverse colors,
possessed of psychic power and radiance.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached with joy the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
The bright ones, the reddish-brown,
and the ruddy ones have come together with the Vepacitti-hosts;
the white-clad ones are at their head.
The wise gods have come:
the Sadāmattas, the Hāragajas,
and the illustrious Missakas.
Pajjunna has come as our son,
he who rains upon all quarters.
These ten [clouds] are tenfold hosts.
All possessed diverse forms;
they were powerful, radiant,
beautiful, and glorious.
Rejoicing, they approached the forest assembly of the bhikkhus—
the Khemiyas, the Tusitas, and the Yāmas.
And the illustrious Kaṭṭhakas;
the Lambītakas, the best of the Lāmas,
and the Āsavas named Joti.
The Nimmanarati devas arrived,
and then the Paranimmita devas arrived;
these ten classes of beings came in ten groups.
All were of diverse complexions;
they possessed psychic power,
radiance, beauty, and glory.
Rejoicing, they approached the forest assembly of the bhikkhus.
These sixty divine hosts—
All were of diverse complexions;
they came according to their names,
as well as others who were similar to them.
"May we behold the Naga, who has shaken off birth,
who is free from blemish, who has crossed the flood,
and who is without taints— the one who ferries others across the flood."
Like the moon surpassing the dark [night].
Subrahmā and Paramatta,
together with the sons of the one possessed of psychic power;
Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa went together to the assembly in the forest;
[there was] a thousand worlds of Brahmā.
Mahābrahmā stands there,
reborn, radiant,
of awe-inspiring form, and glorious.
Ten lords have come here,
each exercising independent power;
and from among them, he has arrived.
Hārita was surrounded by them all—
by the gods, including Indra and Brahmā, who had all approached.
Māra’s army advanced;
behold the folly of Kaṇha!
“Come, seize him! Bind him! they cried.
May you bind him with passion;
surround him on all sides,
and let no one release him.
Thus, thereupon Mahāsena sent forth his army;
striking the palm with his hand, he said:
Having made a terrifying sound,
like a rain-cloud thundering with lightning.
Then he turned back,
agitated and not under his own control;
yet, having directly known all of that, he remained unshaken.
Having established himself,
the Visionary Teacher then addressed his disciples who delight in the teaching.
‘The army of Māra has advanced;
recognize this, O bhikkhus!
And they applied themselves with ardor.
Having heard the Buddha’s teaching,
they departed with their passions gone;
not even a single hair on their bodies stirred.
‘All those who have conquered in battle,
who have transcended fear and possess glory,
rejoice together with all beings.’
“Those disciples of yours were born among men.
The seventh discourse, the Mahāsamaya Sutta, is concluded.
